how: The member calling for a duck also answers the enlargement question, without evidence of appointment to command.
The opening call recruits people to build a duck and later calls ask them to finish it.
A defence appeal receives a brief commitment to help without a request in return.
Members ask whether to enlarge the duck or return to game projects and receive a proposal to complete its body.
Members report an individual pixel contribution and show the completed duck.
A rebuilding participant requests a reference sheet and another supplies an image link.
A shorter cooldown is reported, but neither that report nor the defence appeal establishes scripts, spare accounts, or automated placement.
One member's acceptance and invitations to unseen chat cannot decide whether formal order existed elsewhere or test the model's cross-room frequency claim.
Threat reports recruit defence, overnight care, and immediate help for the duck.
A participant corrects the attributed current attacker from the void to Italians, without demonstrating how the attribution was established.
Neighbouring pixel replacement becomes public offers, conditional restoration, acceptance, and a reported peaceful agreement.
A visitor offers to stop attacking and reports restoring the duck during negotiations.
Participants report help to the duck while requesting help for the flag and Yoshi and directing reciprocal flag repair.
Participants thank allies, honour shared fighting, and apologise for failing to save the shared place.
An alliance to protect both works is offered, named publicly, and accompanied by invitations to shared chat.
A visitor identifies as coming from another subreddit to make a deal and another participant offers to negotiate while defence continues.
Conditional peace and a changed design are visible, but they do not establish a continuing host authority over a guest's territory.
An individual admits accepting the first offer, but no cited passage disputes that individual's right to commit the room.
Calls for help and incomplete repair do not themselves establish a participant's judgment that the room had too few hands.
A participant proposes rebuilding the duck at another location after placement has already ended, showing a proposal rather than an accomplished move.
A proposed restart must remain a proposal when the final canvas cannot change and the proposer acknowledges mistaking closure for a glitch.
A completed duck is announced publicly and its makers later receive thanks.
Members request screenshots, share a last photo, and correct which image represents the final canvas.
Participants mark the ending, mourn missing final representation, and recall a temporary presence that ended before repair.
A participant promises continued alliance in another war, expressing a future tie without establishing its later fulfilment.
The tentative element appears as correction of an incorrectly labelled final image and a hope that later repair will use a preferred reference.
Distinguish checking historical finality from choosing a repair reference, since these passages show neither an executed cleanup nor a dispute over preserving damage.
A surviving title records one author's claim to have added a red dick to the duck.
Treat a visitor's claimed joke alteration as an individual's reported act, without inferring a collective attack by either room or independently verified placement.
A participant reports reciprocal replacement of neighbouring pixels during the building collision.
One participant blames greedy Italians during the last defence effort, supplying an individual hostile attribution rather than evidence of a sustained exchange with a rival.
The pixel collision and the isolated alteration claim supply no pre-canvas tie that could explain the choice of a rival.
The reported collision concerns replacing pixels and does not establish an inherited quarrel.
Choosing a duck and debating its size do not establish the model's stronger claim of acting through inherited lore, ideology, or colour loyalty.
The coded call concerns building on the canvas and supplies no evidence of a host-subreddit April Fools takeover or fake.
Considering a return to videos or game maps supplies no explicit restriction on canvas posting or moderator boundary decision.
The building call receives a report of a pixel contribution, supporting a visible call-and-contribution sequence without measuring silent participation.
The visible starting proposal and call occur together, leaving no distinct earlier start from which to establish the arrow's sequence.
The duck is reported alive before an attack warning and an overnight defence request, supporting an upkeep sequence rather than an independently measured causal effect.
The alarm about Mexico is answered by the same speaker's plan to negotiate while others defend.
Allow restraint and restoration to serve as an offer during negotiation, since restoration is reported before the acceptance rather than only after a settled boundary.
Defence appeals and a shorter cooldown do not reveal a move to machine placement or establish that upkeep exhausted human capacity.
Reporting the duck alive also announces it, and later thanks credit the labour of carving and defence.
Celebration and a screenshot request are visible, but their coexistence does not establish that celebration caused recording.
A last photo and a future-alliance promise coexist without a passage saying that the record caused the promise.
The proposed move is stopped by recognition of closure rather than an expressed judgment of insufficient hands.
Design discussion and a later rebuilding reference are both present, but no coded passage establishes that posting a template settled the earlier design.
The tentative call-to-bare-answer mechanism has a direct local instance when a defence appeal receives an immediate commitment to help.
Reciprocal rebuilding is explicit, but the coded passages do not establish shortage of hands as the cause of seeking outside help.
The public protection agreement is later invoked in instructions to help restore the other party's flag.
The building call, reciprocal overwriting, and a visitor's later alteration claim do not demonstrate that recruited builders were redirected into an attack.
The record supplies a joke alteration claim and negotiation-stage restraint but no observed attack-call-and-refusal pair.
Allow negotiation to answer reciprocal overwriting and a defence alarm without requiring a preceding call to attack the neighbour.
An isolated alteration claim and later hostile attribution do not establish a continuing contest caused by the same attack.
Allow an alliance to form between initially opposing neighbours through an accepted design change, before later common-threat rebuilding.
The building call and an option to return to game projects do not establish a canvas flood or a resulting host posting boundary.
The tentative arrow is not observed because an accepted deal and an individual's retrospective admission do not constitute a dispute over who may commit the room.

statement: welcoming alliance visitors into the room's ordinary activity
how: Alliance contact brings a visitor who asks what the game community is about and receives an explanation of the game, without evidence of lasting membership.
Make recognition of closure a conversational step, since a proposed rebuild receives a finality correction that changes the proposer's understanding.
Include changing the threatened picture into a shared design as a peace term, rather than treating the settlement solely as a line between unchanged works.
Reciprocal rebuilding may be explicitly ordered so that participants restore their own work before returning help to their ally.
